The recursion relation is

$$
f(n+2)=f(n+1)+f(n).
$$

Substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1+2) & =f(1+1)+f(1) \\ f(3) & =f(2)+f(1) \\ f(3) & =(-2)+7 \\ f(3) & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=2$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2+2) & =f(2+1)+f(2) \\ f(4) & =f(3)+f(2) \\ f(4) & =5+(-2) \\ f(4) & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, substituting $n=3,4,5,6$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(5) & =f(3+2)=f(3+1)+f(3)=f(4)+f(3)=3+5=8, \\ f(6) & =f(4+2)=f(4+1)+f(4)=f(5)+f(4)=8+3=11, \\ f(7) & =f(5+2)=f(5+1)+f(5)=f(6)+f(5)=11+8=19, \\ f(8) & =f(6+2)=f(6+1)+f(6)=f(7)+f(6)=19+11=30.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(8)=30.$
